title: The Artin Realizability Direction: the Verifiable Half of the Inverse Galois Problem
description: Isolates and rigorously verifies the elementary part of the inverse Galois problem — Artin's theorem — as the axiom-free counterpart to the axiomatized Shafarevich statement in the parent entry (abel-ruffini-galois-extensions-oq-05). For ANY finite group G acting on a field F, the extension F over its fixed field F^G is Galois (IsGalois.of_fixed_field); and when the action is FAITHFUL, G is isomorphic to the Galois group Gal(F/F^G) (FixedPoints.toAlgAutMulEquiv) with field degree [F : F^G] = |G| (FixedPoints.finrank_eq_card). Bundled as artin_realizability and stated in existence form as realizable_over_some_subfield. The point of the entry is the dividing line it makes precise: realizability over SOME (auxiliary) base field is unconditional and elementary — every finite group is a Galois group over a rational-function-field fixed field via the Cayley/permutation action — whereas the entire depth of Shafarevich's theorem and the open inverse Galois problem is the demand that the base field be ℚ, a fixed arithmetically rigid field. All five results are fully machine-checked, 0 axioms (only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound); the Shafarevich ℚ-realizability axiom is NOT used. This is the first axiom-free realizability result in the abel-ruffini-galois family — all siblings derive their corollaries from the Shafarevich axiom.

meta.assumptions: None added. #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound for every result (extension_isGalois, galoisGroupEquiv, degree_eq_card, artin_realizability, realizable_over_some_subfield). The Shafarevich axiom shafarevich_inverse_galois of the parent entry is NOT used. NOTE on scope: the entry verifies the Artin (fixed-field) direction. The fully unconditional statement 'every finite group is a Galois group over some field' additionally requires that every finite group admit a faithful action on a field — true via the Cayley embedding G ↪ Sym(G) acting on a rational function field K(x_g : g ∈ G), but that construction is described in the docstring rather than formalized here. The realizability theorems below are stated for a finite group already equipped with a faithful field action, which is the precise hypothesis Mathlib's Artin theorem consumes.
originalContributions: artin_realizability: a bundled, axiom-free realizability theorem — a finite group acting faithfully on a field F is the Galois group of F over its fixed field F^G, the extension F/F^G is Galois, and [F : F^G] = |G|. This is the verified counterpart of the parent entry's axiomatized Shafarevich statement, with the base field taken to be F^G rather than ℚ.

realizable_over_some_subfield: the existence form — a finite group acting faithfully on F is the Galois group of F over SOME subfield k ⊆ F, with [F : k] = |G|; the shape that mirrors the inverse-Galois statement 'G is a Galois group over the base' with the base an auxiliary subfield.
extension_isGalois: for any finite group action on a field (faithfulness not required), F/F^G is Galois — the structural backbone, packaging Mathlib's IsGalois.of_fixed_field.

galoisGroupEquiv: the explicit group isomorphism G ≃* Gal(F/F^G) for a faithful finite action, packaging Mathlib's FixedPoints.toAlgAutMulEquiv; degree_eq_card records the matching degree [F : F^G] = |G|.

overview.historicalContext: The inverse Galois problem asks which finite groups arise as Gal(L/ℚ). It splits sharply by base field. Over an auxiliary field one is free to build from the group itself, the answer is elementary and classical: Emil Artin's theorem (1940s; see Artin, 'Galois Theory') says that if a finite group G acts faithfully by automorphisms on a field F, then F/F^G is a finite Galois extension with Galois group exactly G. Combined with the Cayley embedding G ↪ Sym(G) and the permutation action of Sym(G) on a rational function field K(x_g : g ∈ G), this shows every finite group is a Galois group over some field — with no class field theory whatsoever. Over ℚ the problem becomes deep: Shafarevich (1954) proved every finite solvable group is Gal(L/ℚ) using class field theory, embedding problems, and Brauer groups, and the general case remains open. The parent gallery entry abel-ruffini-galois-extensions-oq-05 records Shafarevich's theorem as an axiom; this entry supplies the verified Artin direction that isolates exactly what is hard about ℚ.
overview.problemStatement: Provide the axiom-free, machine-verified counterpart to the parent's axiomatized Shafarevich statement: prove Artin's fixed-field theorem (faithful finite G acting on a field F gives F/F^G Galois with Gal(F/F^G) ≅ G and [F : F^G] = |G|) and present it as the realizability statement over an auxiliary base field, making precise that only the constraint 'base = ℚ' carries the difficulty of the inverse Galois problem.
overview.text: The file packages Mathlib's development of Artin's theorem into a clean realizability statement and contrasts it with the Shafarevich axiom of the parent. extension_isGalois uses IsGalois.of_fixed_field: for any finite group G with a MulSemiringAction on a field F, the fixed field F^G = FixedPoints.subfield G F sits under a Galois extension F/F^G (no faithfulness needed). galoisGroupEquiv uses FixedPoints.toAlgAutMulEquiv: when the action is faithful, the canonical map G → (F ≃ₐ[F^G] F) is a group isomorphism, so G IS the Galois group Gal(F/F^G). degree_eq_card uses FixedPoints.finrank_eq_card to record [F : F^G] = |G|. artin_realizability bundles these three; realizable_over_some_subfield repackages them existentially as 'G is Gal(F/k) for some subfield k with [F:k] = |G|'. The docstring spells out the universal consequence — every finite group is realizable over the fixed field of a faithful Cayley/permutation action on a rational function field — and the dividing line: everything here is 0-axiom, whereas the ℚ-version is the axiom in the parent file.
overview.proofStrategy: Take the genuinely deep input (Artin's fixed-field theorem) from Mathlib's FieldTheory.Fixed and FieldTheory.Galois.Basic, where it is fully proved, and assemble it into the realizability shape that mirrors the inverse Galois statement. State the structural half (F/F^G Galois) for an arbitrary finite action and the realization half (G ≅ Gal(F/F^G), degree |G|) under the faithfulness hypothesis Mathlib's bijectivity result requires. Keep the base field auxiliary (F^G) and flag in the docstring that pinning it to ℚ is exactly the Shafarevich/open content.
keyInsights: Realizability of finite groups as Galois groups is unconditional and elementary over an auxiliary base field — Artin's theorem turns any faithful finite field action into a Galois extension whose group is the acting group. The whole difficulty of the inverse Galois problem is the demand that the base be ℚ.

The structural half (F/F^G is Galois) needs no faithfulness at all: IsGalois.of_fixed_field holds for any finite group action; faithfulness is needed only to identify G with the full Galois group (rather than a quotient) and to pin the degree to |G|.

Cayley + permutation action gives the universal statement: G ↪ Sym(G) acts faithfully on K(x_g : g ∈ G) by permuting variables, so every finite group is a Galois group over the corresponding fixed field — the verified Artin lemmas here are the engine, only the faithful-action construction is left to the docstring.

This is the honest, axiom-free mirror of the parent: where Shafarevich asserts Gal(L/ℚ) ≅ G (axiomatized, class field theory), Artin gives Gal(F/F^G) ≅ G (verified, elementary) — the same conclusion shape with a different, freely-chosen base field.

Existentializing the base is what turns a fixed-field construction into a genuine inverse-Galois statement: artin_realizability names the base concretely as F^G, while realizable_over_some_subfield hides it behind an ∃ k. The two forms carry the same content, but the existence form is precisely the reformulation that isolates 'which base field' as the sole remaining difficulty — everything else (Galois-ness, group identification, degree [F:k]=|G|) is already discharged unconditionally.
prerequisites: Galois extensions L/K (Mathlib IsGalois); the Galois group as the type L ≃ₐ[K] L of K-algebra automorphisms.
Group actions on rings/fields by automorphisms (MulSemiringAction) and the fixed field FixedPoints.subfield G F.
Artin's theorem in Mathlib: IsGalois.of_fixed_field, FixedPoints.toAlgAutMulEquiv, FixedPoints.finrank_eq_card (FieldTheory.Fixed, FieldTheory.Galois.Basic).
Faithful actions (FaithfulSMul) and finiteness (Finite/Fintype); module rank/finrank for the degree formula.
Cayley's theorem (G ↪ Sym(G)) and the permutation action of a symmetric group on a rational function field, for the universal-realizability remark in the docstring.

conclusion.summary: Artin's fixed-field theorem is packaged as a verified, axiom-free realizability statement: a finite group acting faithfully on a field F is the Galois group of F over its fixed field F^G, with F/F^G Galois and [F : F^G] = |G| (artin_realizability, realizable_over_some_subfield). The structural half F/F^G Galois holds for any finite action (extension_isGalois). All results are 0-axiom (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only); the Shafarevich axiom is not used. 4 theorems, 1 definition, 97 lines.
conclusion.implications: Together with the parent entry this draws the precise line in the inverse Galois problem: the realization of finite groups as Galois groups is elementary over an auxiliary base field (Artin, verified here) and becomes deep only when the base is forced to be ℚ (Shafarevich, axiomatized in the parent; general case open). The Artin lemmas are reusable for any concrete faithful field action; supplying the Cayley/permutation action on a rational function field would upgrade realizable_over_some_subfield to the unconditional 'every finite group is a Galois group over some field'.
openQuestions: Formalize the universal corollary: every finite group G is a Galois group over some field, by constructing the faithful action of G (via Cayley G ↪ Sym(G)) on the rational function field K(x_g : g ∈ G) and extending the variable-permutation action of Sym(G) on MvPolynomial to its fraction field, then applying realizable_over_some_subfield.

Replace the auxiliary base field F^G by ℚ for specific solvable groups (cyclic, abelian) using cyclotomic fields and the Kronecker–Weber theorem — discharging the cyclic/abelian corollaries of the parent without the Shafarevich axiom.

Strengthen extension_isGalois to record the surjection G ↠ Gal(F/F^G) for a non-faithful finite action, with kernel the ineffective part of the action, recovering the faithful case as the injective specialization.

sections.title: Overview and imports
sections.summary: Module docstring framing the entry as the verified Artin counterpart of the axiomatized Shafarevich parent: states the fixed-field theorem, the universal-realizability consequence via Cayley + permutation action on a rational function field, and the dividing line that pins the inverse Galois difficulty entirely to the base field being ℚ. Imports Mathlib; opens MulSemiringAction.

sections.title: Section I — F/F^G is Galois (any finite action)
sections.summary: extension_isGalois: for any finite group G with a MulSemiringAction on a field F, IsGalois (FixedPoints.subfield G F) F, via Mathlib's IsGalois.of_fixed_field. No faithfulness is required — this is the structural backbone of the realization.

sections.title: Section II — G is the Galois group, with degree |G|
sections.summary: galoisGroupEquiv: for a faithful finite action, the group isomorphism G ≃* (F ≃ₐ[F^G] F) (FixedPoints.toAlgAutMulEquiv). degree_eq_card: [F : F^G] = |G| (FixedPoints.finrank_eq_card). Together: G is exactly Gal(F/F^G), and the extension degree matches the group order.

sections.title: Section III — bundled realizability
sections.summary: artin_realizability bundles the three facts of Sections I–II into one statement for a faithful finite action: IsGalois (F^G) F ∧ (G ≃* Gal(F/F^G)) ∧ [F:F^G] = |G|, proved simply as ⟨extension_isGalois, ⟨galoisGroupEquiv⟩, degree_eq_card⟩. This is the verified, axiom-free counterpart of the Shafarevich axiom in the parent file, with the base taken to be F^G rather than ℚ.
sections.mathContext: For a finite $G$ acting faithfully on $F$: $\mathrm{IsGalois}\,F^G\,F \ \wedge\ G \cong \mathrm{Gal}(F/F^G)\ \wedge\ [F:F^G]=|G|$.

sections.title: Section IV — existence form (inverse-Galois shape)
sections.summary: realizable_over_some_subfield repackages the bundle existentially: a finite group acting faithfully on F is the Galois group of F over *some* subfield k ⊆ F with [F:k] = |G| (witnessed by k = F^G). This is the shape that mirrors the inverse Galois statement 'G is a Galois group over the base' — here the base is an auxiliary subfield rather than ℚ, which is exactly what makes it unconditional.
sections.mathContext: $\exists\,k \subseteq F$ a subfield with $\mathrm{IsGalois}\,k\,F$, $G \cong \mathrm{Gal}(F/k)$, and $[F:k]=|G|$ — realized by $k=F^G$.

crossReferences.description: Parent: records Shafarevich's theorem (every finite solvable group is Gal(L/ℚ)) as an axiom and derives corollaries from it. This entry supplies the axiom-free Artin direction — the same realization shape Gal(F/base) ≅ G with the base an auxiliary fixed field rather than ℚ — isolating ℚ as the entire source of difficulty.

Grandparent: proves S_n is solvable iff n ≤ 4 and the Abel–Ruffini necessity direction. Artin realizability is the field-theoretic engine behind 'every finite group is some field's Galois group', complementing the radical-solvability story.

The general inverse Galois problem over ℚ. Artin's theorem shows the problem is trivial over auxiliary base fields; the open ℚ-version is what this entry's docstring identifies as the residual difficulty.
